memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The third lot came up for Zebulun according to its clans: The boundary of their inheritance went as far as Sarid. Going west it ran to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and extended to the ravine near Jokneam. It turned east from Sarid toward the sunrise to the territory of Kisloth Tabor and went on to Daberath and up to Japhia - Josh 19:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The third lot falls to Zebulun, and its borders are traced through the region of Galilee in the north. To most readers these place names mean little, but this is worth noticing: Zebulun's territory lay in the very area where, centuries later, Jesus would grow up and begin His ministry. Nazareth, Cana, and the shores of Galilee all lay in or near this land. The gospel would first shine in the region assigned here to Zebulun.

The prophet Isaiah spoke of exactly this. He foretold that the land of Zebulun, which had known darkness and gloom, would one day see a great light (Isa 9:1-2). And Matthew tells us plainly that this was fulfilled when Jesus came and began preaching in Galilee (Matt 4:13-16). The ordinary tribal allotment recorded here was, unknown to Zebulun, being marked out as the stage for the dawning of the Messiah's light.

How wonderful that God was weaving His redemptive plan through a simple land grant. Zebulun received its portion long before anyone knew what glory would one day rise there. It reminds us that God is always working further ahead than we can see. The ordinary circumstances of our lives may be part of a plan whose fullness we cannot yet imagine. The God who prepared Galilee for the light of Christ is quietly preparing good things in our lives too, for His glory (Eph 3:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does it amaze you that God prepared Zebulun's land for Christ's ministry long before?
- How does God's working "further ahead than we can see" encourage you?
- Where might God be preparing something in your ordinary circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You work further ahead than I can see, as You prepared Galilee for the light of Christ. Help me to trust Your unseen purposes in my ordinary days. Amen.
